Cc: VelaFi SRE <sre@velafi.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jan 2029 16:12:00 -0500
Subject: Unexpected throughput drop on Reserved - production impact

Hi Rishi,

We started seeing a sustained backlog on our reserved capacity around 09:00 PT (~3 hours ago). Token latency for critical endpoints (account reconciliation, scoring) climbed from 45ms median to 480ms and 5xx rates hit ~2.8% across the cluster. The customer-facing errors are causing retries and a visible increase in user churn on the payment flow.

Attached is a screenshot of the service graphs (svc_metrics.png) and a short tail-sample of KV cache evictions. We did a quick verify on our side and don't see any spike in QPS from our clients that would explain the severity.

Can you confirm whether this is noisy neighboring on your dedicated GPU pool or something in the reserved routing? We are on the DF-4821 reserved plan. This is affecting production; we need an immediate remediation plan and — if required — a temporary capacity burst while you investigate.

Next steps we need:
- Immediate triage and visible timeline (30m SLA please)
- Temporary burst/provisioning if headroom is exhausted
- Post-mortem and potential SLA credit if this turns into a >4hr outage

Thanks — Lina
Lina Park
Head of Platform Reliability, VelaFi

Lina — thanks for the signal and the graphs. I see the same headroom pressure in our telemetry for your reserved pool (DF-4821). I'm escalating immediately and copying ops and account leadership.

What we are doing now (30m ops window):
- Triage live (Irene + infra) to identify if this is noisy neighbor, KV cache thrash, or kernel-level saturation.
- If the pool is saturated, we will propose a quick Dedicated burst for 4–6 hours to restore tail latency while we mitigate.
- If a routing/regression is found, we will push an urgent rollback.

Please confirm: are you able to take a short traffic-shed (5–10%) for a 15-minute test if we try a fallback routing? If not, we will proceed with burst authorization request to avoid user impact.

I'll follow up with a diagnostic summary within 20–30 minutes.

—Rishi

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 22 Jan 2029 16:52:00 -0500
Subject: Fwd: Unexpected throughput drop on Reserved - quick findings and ask

Forwarding initial ops notes and findings. Quick summary:
- Observed: sustained token-queue depth and KV cache miss-rate increased 6x starting ~08:55 PT.
- Root cause (likely): attacker-like pattern / sudden shift in payload size distribution causing KV cache churn and inefficient kernel scheduling on a subset of DGX nodes. Noise concentrated on nodes 12–15 in pool DF-4821.
- Impact: median token latency increased, tail spiked; a handful of requests hit 5xx due to OOM retries on the worker.

Immediate mitigation options (pick one):
1) Temporary Dedicated burst (3 extra instances on nearest region) for 6 hours while we rehydrate KV cache and migrate noisy tenants. Requires exec sign-off for emergency capacity billing (we can credit if needed).
2) Apply soft-rate-limit to non-critical endpoints and shift critical traffic to a lower-latency routing node (requires VelaFi agreement to shed 10% traffic for 15 minutes).
3) Emergency rolling kernel rollback on affected nodes (risk: ~5–10% increased latency briefly during migration).

Recommended: Option 1 while we enact Option 3. Rationale: quickest customer-facing relief and gives ops breathing room to do a clean migration.

Requesting Marissa / Hannah: can we get emergency authorization to apply a Dedicated burst for VelaFi (DF-4821) up to 6 hours and auto-approve any credits later? If not, we need an exec call with billing and the customer.

Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
